sections.h2: Which ways of selling work for a Burton homeowner?
sections.html:
Choices in Burton run from a standard listing, to a private sale, to a cash deal with someone ready to absorb whatever work the house needs. All of them end with a deed recorded at the Genesee County Register of Deeds and transfer tax paid on the price.

Pick the route by looking at three things: how soon you must be out, what condition the house is in, and whether anything stands in the way of a clean title, such as back taxes, a lien or an unfinished estate. Patience and a house that shows well favor a listing. A seller who needs a firm date is better served by cash.

  • Agent listing: more buyers, but showings, appraisal and a buyer's lender add delay.
  • Private sale: no listing fee, with the paperwork on you.
  • Cash sale: fewer steps, and the buyer handles repairs after closing.

sections.h2: What should a seller notice about Burton itself?
sections.html:
Burton lies just outside Flint in Genesee County, and its roughly 29,300 residents make it the county's second largest city. It was Burton Township from 1856 and became a city in 1972 after residents voted to incorporate. The city covers roughly 23 square miles of land.

Two named neighborhoods show how the area is laid out. Belsay lies on Belsay Road at the rail line north of I-69 and Court Street, and Lapeer Heights sits at Belsay and Roberta Roads south of Lapeer Road.

One recent change matters for utility costs: Burton began receiving Karegnondi Water Authority water, treated by the Genesee County Drain Commission, in December 2017. A buyer comparing monthly costs may ask about water bills, so keep a recent statement handy.

sections.h2: How does Burton's housing picture look in Census data?
sections.html:
Burton is a city of homeowners, with more than three in four households owning. The Census Bureau's figures are below.

A population share of nearly one in five aged 65 or older means a good share of owners may be weighing a move to smaller housing or have inherited a house. If that is your situation, start by confirming who has legal authority to sign the deed.

sections.h2: How did Burton grow, and how does age show up in its houses?
sections.html:
Burton's population jumped from 2,154 in 1920 to 29,700 in 1960, and the census peak came in 1970 at 32,540. That growth points to a housing stock built largely in the mid-twentieth century. The count has drifted down since, to 29,715 in 2020 and an estimated 29,313 in 2025.

Early settlers arrived from Jefferson County, New York, and the first community was the Atherton settlement on Thread Creek in 1835. Over the years Flint annexed large pieces of the township's northern and western sides, which shaped the city's present boundaries.

For a seller, a house from the 1950s or 1960s can mean older plumbing, an aging furnace and a modest garage. The climate is humid continental, with warm summers and cold winters, so heating systems and roofs deserve attention before showings. Disclose what you know about them, and keep receipts for any work done.

sections.h2: Which Burton permit rules should you check before a sale?
sections.html:
Burton's Building Division publishes plain rules that decide whether past work will cause trouble with a buyer. The owner is responsible for making sure a permit was pulled, and unpermitted work can come up in an inspection or in the buyer's lender review.

  • A shed under 199 square feet needs a site permit; a structure of 200 square feet or more counts as a garage and needs a building permit.
  • Decks need permits unless they stand free at least 10 feet from the house and are under 200 square feet.
  • Finishing a basement requires a permit and an egress window.
  • In-ground pools need permits, and above-ground pools do when they stay up year round.
  • Cosmetic interior work such as paint and flooring needs no permit.

If you built a deck or finished the basement yourself, call the Building Division through City Hall and ask what is on file. Closing that gap before listing is cheaper than negotiating it afterward.

sections.h2: How do Burton property taxes work when a house sells?
sections.html:
Burton bills twice a year on deadlines of its own. Summer bills go out by July 1 and are due by September 30, and a one-time 4% penalty applies on October 1 with half a percent a month after that. Winter bills go out December 1 and are due by February 28. The city does not accept postmarks, so payment has to arrive at the Treasurer's office at 4303 S. Center Road by the due date.

On March 1 the account moves to the Genesee County Treasurer (810-257-3054), where a 4% collection fee and rising interest apply. The city states that property unpaid after two years is foreclosed and sold at auction.

The city's tax page also explains Proposal A: taxable value is capped at the lesser of inflation or 5% a year while the owner stays, but it can rise to the state equalized value after a transfer. A buyer's first bill can therefore exceed yours. New principal residence exemption applications reach the assessor by June 1, and a change of residence calls for an update form.

sections.h2: What are the Genesee County recording charges?
sections.html:
Recording at the Genesee County Register of Deeds costs a $30 flat fee for each document, whatever its length. Warranty deeds, land contracts and any deed containing a covenant of warranty need a $5 tax certification from the Genesee County Treasurer, paid by a separate check.

The county's fee page lists $7.50 per thousand for the state and $1.10 per thousand for the county, which add up to $8.60. The seller is liable and the base is the price paid, so a $140,000 sale produces $1,204. Mortgages carry no transfer tax in Michigan.

A few transfers escape the tax, such as a gift deed to your child or a deed given in lieu of foreclosure, and the deed itself has to cite the exemption.

sections.h2: Is a cash buyer right for your Burton sale?
sections.html:
It can be, once the work a retail buyer would demand costs more than the discount a cash buyer applies. That happens with houses needing a roof or mechanical work, estates with several heirs, and landlord-owned houses with unpaid rent.

Gather your tax bill, any permit records and a recent water statement, and ask each buyer for a written offer that spells out who pays closing costs. Line up at least two before you sign anything.

faqs.q: Does Burton demand an inspection before closing?
faqs.a: The Building Division grants building, site and occupancy permits. Ask it through City Hall whether your address needs any occupancy sign-off or has open permits before closing.

faqs.q: What does transfer tax cost on a Burton sale?
faqs.a: Genesee County posts a combined $8.60 for each $1,000 of price. At $120,000 that is $1,032, owed by the seller under the statute unless an exemption applies.

faqs.q: What are Burton's property tax deadlines?
faqs.a: Summer taxes are due by September 30 and winter taxes by February 28, according to the city Treasurer. After March 1, unpaid taxes go to the Genesee County Treasurer with added fees and interest.

faqs.q: Will unpermitted work block a Burton sale?
faqs.a: Not automatically, but expect questions. Permits are the owner's duty, and a buyer may ask for a discount or want the work legalized. A cash buyer usually accepts the condition and adjusts the price.

faqs.q: What becomes of my homestead exemption in a Burton sale?
faqs.a: It ends once the house is no longer your principal residence. Michigan expects a Request to Rescind (Form 2602) at the city assessor within 90 days, and lateness costs $5 a day up to $200.
